hero.title: Excessive Oil Consumption UK Causes, Repair Costs & Fixes
hero.description: Burning oil has multiple potential causes - from a £100 PCV valve to a £3,000+ piston ring rebuild . Blue smoke from your exhaust doesn't automatically mean your engine is scrap. The key is proper diagnosis before assuming the worst. Many owners have paid for a full rebuild when a £150 PCV valve would have fixed the problem.

blocks.text: If your oil light comes on (red oil can symbol), stop driving immediately.
The oil light indicates critically low oil pressure, not just low level. Driving with the oil light on will destroy bearings within minutes, leading to engine seizure (£2,500-£6,500+).

blocks.text: Specialist rule of thumb: "90% of oil consumption complaints on turbocharged engines are either a blocked PCV valve or worn valve stem seals. A PCV valve is a £150 part and an hour's labour. A piston ring rebuild is £3,000. Always diagnose from the cheapest possibility upward."

No blue smoke but oil level drops

blocks.text: The maths of ignoring: Fix immediately (PCV valve): £100-£250. Wait 6 months (valve seals): £500-£1,500. Wait 12 months (piston rings or engine): £1,500-£6,500.

rows: Always - check manufacturer spec (BMW LL-04, VW 507.00)

blocks.text: Cost ranges [INDUSTRY ESTIMATE]. Labour: PCV 1-2 hrs, valve seals 6-10 hrs, rings 12-20 hrs, turbo 4-8 hrs at £65-£95/hr indie.

Vehicle Value Threshold: Under £2,000 - PCV only. If valve seals or rings, evaluate scrap. £2,000-£4,000 - Valve seals or turbo viable. Rings? Evaluate carefully. £4,000-£8,000 - Piston ring rebuild or replacement engine justified. £8,000+ - Any repair - even full engine rebuild.

Specialist rule of thumb: "The single biggest cause of oil consumption on modern engines is using the wrong oil spec. A BMW needs LL-04. A VW needs 507.00. Put cheap oil in, and it will burn it. Put the right oil in, and consumption often stops."

cards.text: What causes a car to burn oil? + Blocked PCV valve (cheapest), worn valve stem seals (blue smoke on start-up), worn piston rings (blue smoke on acceleration), turbo seals leaking, wrong oil grade, or external oil leaks.
cards.fullText: What causes a car to burn oil? + Blocked PCV valve (cheapest), worn valve stem seals (blue smoke on start-up), worn piston rings (blue smoke on acceleration), turbo seals leaking, wrong oil grade, or external oil leaks.

cards.text: How do I know if I need piston rings or just valve seals? + Blue smoke only on cold start = valve stem seals (£500-£1,500). Blue smoke on acceleration = piston rings or turbo (£1,500-£4,000+). A compression test confirms. Don't pay for rings without this test.

cards.text: Is it worth fixing oil consumption on an old car? + If your car is worth £2,000-£4,000 and the fix is valve seals (£500-£1,500), yes. If under £2,000 and needs rings (£1,500-£4,000+), evaluate scrap first. → Repair vs replacement
